title: Why Katyushas Rode Wooden Sleds
topic: Why the Soviet Union launched the “Katyusha” rocket launchers on wooden sleds in 1941 to facilitate rapid mobility across snowy terrain

lines: The weapon was top secret, and it had to move fast.
The artillery branch hated these launchers.
Loading and firing 24 rockets took up to 50 minutes.
A conventional howitzer could fire 95 to 150 rounds in the same time.
The Katyusha was fragile compared to artillery guns.
It had to fire a large blow all at once, then move before being located and attacked with counter-battery fire.
It was mounted on many platforms during World War II, including trucks, artillery tractors, tanks, and armoured trains.
You see, it’s like trying to push a heavy cart through deep snow.
A sled spreads the weight and slides over the top.
So the Katyusha was mounted on many platforms, including sledges.
The sledges let the crew move the launcher across snow to a new spot.
The Katyusha was cheap, easy to produce, and usable on almost any chassis.
That mobility let it deliver a large blow all at once, then move before being located.
